existing_api.owner: DT current model replay and FSDP boundary
facts: Replay callback is called unchanged; the owner retains only the current replayed layer gathered weights for its following finite consumer, then restores original FSDP settings.
No sequence/chunk/dtype argument exists on this replay boundary.
Existing root checkpoint bank copies per-layer activations and kwargs to CPU; this is not an all-layer GPU activation bank.

facts: Capture destination can be CPU, and the copy owner preserves tensor dtype. Borrowing same-device copy=False returns the detached original storage.
Actual retained capture backend delegates to this owner with copy=False; gate/up/silu borrows extend native output lifetimes without allocating copies.
App628 L416 and Text5f14 L414 explicitly select decoder destination cuda. Mixer offload/restore is a separate current API.
existing_api.direct_applicability: Current finite MLP directly consumes complete gate/up/silu tensors on their present device. There is no exposed decoder CPU destination option plus matching current decoder restore/chunk-bank consumer; changing the constructor destination alone is not a complete supported execution path.

confirmed_interface_gap: The configured original native MLP replay has no token chunk hook despite the official generic helper existing in the installed package.

DT capture hooks retain each name by assignment, and current runner requires each decoder/gate/up/silu/down/mlp call count equal one. Direct multi-chunk original MLP calls would overwrite prior chunk values and fail this existing coverage check; capture assembly/consumer semantics are not currently supplied.
App finite 2048 chunking bounds only the later finite rule. It does not bound original HF/PEFT base/LoRA/scaling/add temporaries that failed before finite_decoder.
A CPU decoder capture destination primitive exists, but no complete current decoder offload/restore consumer interface was found. It cannot by itself remove the original PEFT intermediate at L807.
dtype_and_lifetime_facts: HF post_attention_layernorm returns type_as(x) at L767; Qwen MLP contains no explicit forced activation dtype.

PEFT L793 retains base result and L794 records its dtype; L805 sends x through _cast_input_dtype using LoRA_A.weight.dtype. BaseTunerLayer L1550–1553 returns x unchanged for matching dtype or disabled cast; otherwise x.to(dtype) may allocate a full input-shaped tensor.

PEFT L807 computes original LoRA A/B, scaling and addition while base result is live, then L818 casts the completed result back to the base result dtype. Final BF16 projection output would therefore not prove the intermediates were BF16.

Pinned PEFT cast_adapter_dtype can upcast half/BF16 adapter parameters to FP32. Source availability/default alone does not establish current actual adapter parameter or branch result dtype; original FSDP mixed precision and any active autocast also matter.

NativeDecoderCapture detach/to destination preserves dtype. The actual same-device retain backend does not downcast gate/up/silu; borrowed captures can keep gate storage live during up_proj LoRA temporaries and all three until finite MLP consumption.

App finite consumer releases gate/up/silu after boundaries.mlp and releases post_norm_input after norm residual. Current layer weights are released after finite decoder. These later lifetime boundaries cannot prevent an allocation failure in native PEFT before the projection post-hook.

Logical full gate/up/silu payload is P*T*I*(element_size(gate)+element_size(up)+element_size(silu)); actual resident bytes require actual distinct storage, strides, dtypes and P/T. No failing P/T or FP32 assumption is introduced.

measurement_dependent_selection.facts_needed: Use the already armed passive native owner hooks for actual layer, input/base/LoRA_A/LoRA_B/projection output shapes, dtypes and storage identities. No additional model invocation was performed by this audit.
measurement_dependent_selection.why: Those fields distinguish native LoRA temporary width from retained full captures and determine which already available owner primitive addresses the actual peak. The historical allocation size alone cannot reconstruct all dimensions or dtype.
